cards.headline: The Taylor Swift rumor, and what Charli said it was really about
cards.snippet: When Charli XCX's album Brat came out in June 2024, fans guessed that "Sympathy Is a Knife" was about Taylor Swift and her ex Matty Healy of the 1975. Talk grew when Swift reissued The Tortured Poets Department in the UK the week after Brat's release, which fans saw as an effort to block Brat from number one. Charli confirmed there were no "diss tracks" on Brat and denied the song was about Swift. She said it was about her anxiety, insecurities and wanting to avoid situations that make her doubt herself.
cards.context: Speculation grew when Swift reissued her album in the UK the week after Brat's release.

cards.headline: A crowd chanted "Taylor is dead!" and Charli shut it down
cards.snippet: In June 2024, Charli XCX was playing a DJ set in São Paulo when the audience began chanting "A Taylor morreu!", Portuguese for "Taylor is dead!". The chant came amid fan speculation that "Sympathy Is a Knife" targeted Taylor Swift. Charli later posted on her Instagram story asking fans to stop and said she "will not tolerate it". In an August 2024 Vulture interview, Swift praised Charli's musical sensibilities and called her writing "surreal and inventive, always".
cards.context: Swift later praised Charli's writing in a Vulture interview.

cards.headline: The remix is about a different kind of pain: being scrutinized
cards.snippet: When Charli XCX released the Ariana Grande remix of "Sympathy Is a Knife" in October 2024, it shifted to public scrutiny. Talking to Zane Lowe on Apple Music 1, Charli said her perspective had changed since Brat first came out. During the album's campaign, some interviews left her feeling manipulated or sensing other agendas, which she had never felt before. When she heard Grande wanted to work on the song, she thought Grande would know that feeling better than she did.
cards.context: Charli told Zane Lowe on Apple Music 1 that her perspective had changed since the album's release.
